title: Raghav Aditya Chits (P). Ltd. vs . Nazar Mohammad on 17 March, 2023
full_text: Raghav Aditya Chits (P). Ltd. vs . Nazar Mohammad on 17 March, 2023 IN THE COURT OF SH. PANKAJ RAI METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE ­05 (N.I. ACT), ROUSE AVENUE COURT: NEW DELHI DISTRICT CC No. 1823/2020 Raghav Aditya Chits (P). Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad 1. Complaint Case number : 1823/2020 2 Name and address of : M/s. Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. the complainant registered office at : B­32, Regency Park, DLF Phase­IV, Gurugram, Haryana. Collection Office in Delhi at: 8­A, Partap Market, Munirka, New Delhi­110067. 3. Name and address of : Nazar Mohammad the accused S/o Sh. Rahmatullah, R/o H.No. 61­A, Kalu Sarai, New Delhi­110016. 4. Offence complained of : Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. 5. Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty and claim trial. 6. Final Order : Acquitted 7. Date of Institution : 03.02.2020 8. Date of Reserving the : 25.02.2023 Judgment 9. Date of pronouncement : 17.03.2023 JUDGMENT: 1. Vide this judgment I shall dispose of the complaint filed by the complainant under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act '). C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.1/17 2. Brief facts relevant for the decision of the case are as under:­ The complainant company alleges that it is engaged in the business of chit funds in the state of Haryana. That the accused approached and requested the complainant to become subscriber of a chit group run by it. That the accused also agreed and undertook to abide by the terms and conditions of the chit group no. P­1, ticket no. 13 and chit group no O­10, ticket no. 18. both chits having total value of Rs.10,00,000/­ and that both the chit groups started from the month of September, 2011 for a period of 40 months. That the accused became the successful bidder of chit group no.O­10 for ticket no.18 and was paid by the complainant the prized amount of Rs.6,00,000/­. That the accused also became the successful bidder of chit group no.P­1 for ticket no.13 and was paid by the complainant the prized amount of Rs.6,00,000/­. That both chits amount was repayable by the accused in 40 monthly installments of Rs.25,000/­ each. That the accused made the payments against 32 monthly installments for the period of September 2011 uptill April,2014 and that the accused failed to pay eight (8) installments of Rs.25,000/­ each of both the chit groups and that a sum of Rs.4,00,000/­ was thus due and payable by the accused to the complainant. That the accused was also liable to pay Rs.4,48,000/­ towards interest @ 24% per annum on the above mentioned outstanding dues from the month of Jnauary, 2015 till August, 2019 and that the complainant was also entitled to future interest @24% on the above outstanding amount. That the complainant through its agents and representatives has visited the C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.2/17 accused several times and requested for the payment of above outstanding dues. That, thereafter, upon the receipt of a legal notice dated 10.09.2019 from the complainant, the accused issued the cheque in question bearing no. 140941 dated 16.12.2019 for an amount of Rs.7,75,000/­ drawn on Oriental Bank of Commerce, Sarvpriya Vihar, Kalu Sarai, New Delhi in favour of the complainant with an assurance of its encashment. The complainant presented the cheque in its account maintained at Canara Bank, Munirka Branch, New Delhi which was returned with the remarks "account closed and transferred" vide bank return memo dated 18.12.2019. That, thereafter, complainant served a legal notice dated 23.12.2019 Ex.CW1/15 upon the accused through its counsel demanding the said amount. Despite service of aforesaid notice, neither any reply was sent nor the money was repaid by the accused. Thereafter, complainant has filed the present complaint case with the submission that accused be summoned, tried and punished according to law. 3. In its pre­summoning evidence, the AR of the complainant was examined on affidavit Ex. CW­1/A. He reiterated the contents of complaint and placed on record the following documents namely: (a) Mark A : Certificate of incorporation of complainant and e­form 18; (b) Ex. CW1/1 : Board resolution in favour of AR of the complainant; (c) Ex. CW1/2 (OSR) : Copy of agreement dated 16.11.2011; C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.3/17 (d) Ex. CW1/3 (OSR) : Copy of demand promissary note dated 16.11.2011; (e) Ex. CW1/4 (Colly) (OSR) : Cash vouchers, receipts / acknowledgement dated 16.11.2011. (f) Ex. CW1/5 (OSR) : Copy of agreement dated 01.04.2013. (g) Ex. CW1/6 (OSR) : Copy of demand promissary note dated 01.04.2013; (h) Ex. CW1/7 (Colly) (OSR) : Cash vouchers, receipts / acknowledgement dated 01.04.2013. (i) Ex. CW1/8 and Ex. CW1/9 : Copy of payments received from the accused towards installments. (j) Ex. CW1/10 : Office copy of legal notice dated 10.09.2019; (k) Ex. CW1/11 (colly) : Original postal receipts of the above notice; (l) Ex. CW1/12 (Colly) : Copy of tracking reports thereof; (m) Ex. CW1/13 : Cheque in question bearing no. 140941; (n) Ex. CW1/14 : Cheque dishonour memo; (o) Ex.CW1/15 : Office copy of legal demand notice dated 23.12.2019; C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.4/17 (p) Ex. CW1/16 (Colly) : Original postal receipts; and (q) Ex. CW1/17 (Colly) : Copy of postal tracking report. 4. Upon appreciation of pre­summoning evidence, accused was summoned for an offence punishable under Section 138 of the Act and notice under Section 251 Cr.P.C. for this offence was framed upon accused on 01.04.2021 to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. He admitted his signatures on the cheque in question. He stated that he had issued the cheque in connection with a chit to the complainant and that he had issued total eight cheques to the complainant and that they were never returned back to him by the complainant despite his repeated demand multiple times and that he has already repaid the amount to the complainant in cash in connection with the chit fund. 5. The accused moved an application to cross­examine the AR of the complainant as CW­1 and that the AR was duly cross examined by the accused on 19.07.2022 and 30.09.2022. No other witness was produced by the complainant and the complainant evidence was closed. Thereafter, statement of accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded on 07.11.2022 in which all the incriminating evidence were put to him to which accused stated that he had subscribed to the aforesaid chit fund of the complainant and that he is an illetrate person and that he got the chit amount of Rs. 6 Lacs each twice in the year 2011. That he has not received any alleged payment from the complainant in the year 2013. He admitted that both the chit amount were repayable by him in 40 monthly C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.5/17 installments of Rs. 25,000/­ each for every chit group and that he had already repaid the entire amount by the year 2014. He admitted the receipt of legal demand notice Ex.CW1/15 from the complainant. The accused further stated that he want to lead defence evidence. However, vide separate statement of accused recorded on 15.02.2023 DE was closed. Thereafter, matter was listed for final arguments. Final arguments were heard on behalf of both the parties. 6. It was argued by the Ld. counsel for the complainant that this is a fit case for conviction of the accused as all the essential ingredients of Section 138 of the Act read with Section 139 of the Act have been fulfilled and that the same has been aptly demonstrated by the complainant before the court. That the accused had subscribed to the chit group run by the complainant and that the accused had never disputed the subscription of above chit group of the complainant. That the receipt of legal demand notice has been admitted by the accused in his statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. That the accused has failed to furnish any proof that he had paid all the installments to the complainant. That the accused admitted his signatures on the cheque in question in answer to notice under section 251 Cr.P.C. It is finally submitted that accused failed to raise the probable defence to disprove the case of complainant and to rebut the presumption under Section 139 of the Act. Therefore, accused be convicted for the offence under Section 138 of the Act. 7. Per contra, Ld. Counsel for the accused has argued that the C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.6/17 present debt/liability is time barred as admittedly the last payment was received by the complainant from the accused on 27.06.2014 and that the time period of three years for recovery of amount against the accused expired somewhere in July, 2017 whereas the present complaint was filed by the complainant on 31.01.2020 which is much beyond the period of limitation of three years for recovery of the outstanding amount and hence the alleged debt was time barred and is not legally recoverable herein. That the accused had not made any acknowldgement of debt in favour of the complainant within the period of limitation. It is also submitted that the complainant has failed to produce on record its balance sheet and books of accounts to show the liability of the accused for the cheque amount. He further relies upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Jage Ram Karan Singh & Anr Vs State & Anr decided on 31.07.2019 to contend that the cheque issued for a time barred liability is not covered under section 138 NI Act. He further submitted that the complainant has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and accused is entitled to be acquitted of offence u/s 138 of the Act as probable defence has been raised by the accused and sufficient doubt has been created on the version of the complainant. 8. Record perused. There is no dispute regarding the propositions of law laid down in the judgments relied upon by the parties. 9. For the offence under Section 138 of the Act to be made out against the accused, the complainant must prove the following points, C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.7/17 that:­ (i) the accused issued a cheque on account maintained by him with a bank. (ii) the said cheque had been issued in discharge, in whole or in part, of any legal debt or other liability. (iii) the said cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of three months from the date of cheque or within the period of its validity. (iv) the aforesaid cheque, when presented for encashment, was returned unpaid/dishonoured. (v) the payee of the cheque issued a legal notice of demand to the drawer within 30 days from the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque. (vi) the drawer of the cheque failed to make the payment within 15 days of the receipt of aforesaid legal notice of demand. 10. The main question which is to be adjudicated by this court is as to whether the accused, on a scale of preponderance of probabilities, has shown that there exists no legally recoverable debt against him or not. 11. The AR of the complainant, by way of an affidavit, led his evidence C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.8/17 as CW­1 testifying that cheque in question was issued to the complainant for a valid and enforceable debt. The cheque in question, dishonour memo of the cheque and legal demand notice were exhibited on record. I straightaway come to the issue of existence of legal liability upon the accused. In the case in hand, the facts of issuance of the cheque, signatures of accused on the cheque and receipt of legal demand notice by the accused is not disputed. In a case under Negotiable Instrument Act , the complainant need not to prove the existence of liability as once these facts that the cheque in question belongs to the accused and the signature on the cheque in question are of the accused are established, a presumption of the cheque having been issued in discharge of a legally sustainable liability and drawn for good consideration, arises by virtue of Section 118 (a) and Section 139 of the NI Act and the court presumes that the cheque was issued in discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or their liability. At this stage, with the help of the presumption under Section 139 of the Act, the case of the complainant stands proved. When the presumption is raised in favor of the complainant, the burden shifts upon the accused to disprove the case of the complainant by rebutting the presumption raised in favour of the complainant. Being the rule of reverse onus, it is the duty on the accused to prove that he does not owe any liability towards the complainant. The accused can displace this presumption on the scale of preponderance of probabilities by raising a probable defence and the lack of consideration or a legally enforceable debt need not be proved beyond all reasonable doubts. The accused has to make out a fairly plausible defence which is acceptable to the court. This the accused can do either by leading own evidence in his defence, C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.9/17 or by raising doubt on the material/evidence brought on the record by the complainant. For this, reliance is placed upon the judgment of Apex Court in case title Rangappa Vs. Sri Mohan ( 2010) 11 SCC 441 and Kumar Exports vs Sharma Carpets (2009) 2 SCC 513. 12. Even otherwise, it is an established principle of criminal law that unlike the complainant, the accused is not required to prove his defence beyond all reasonable doubt and has to merely establish a reasonable doubt in the case of the complainant as noted above. Further, the explanation to section 138 is categorical that for the purposes of section 138 , "debt or other legal liability" means legally enforceable debt or other liability. 13. The Ld. Counsel for the complainant argued that the accused has admitted in his statement under section 313 of CrPC that he had subscribed to the chit groups of the complainant and that he has also received the prized amount from the complainant and that he had also admitted his signatures on the documents regarding the execution of promissory note and receipt of acknowledgment of bid amount in terms of Ex.CW1/3 (OSR) and Ex.CW1/4 (Colly)(OSR). Further the issuance of the cheque in question to the complainant is not denied and it is not the case of the accused that the cheque in question has been obtained by the complainant through, fraud or coercion. The Ld. Counsel for the complainant also contended that although the accused has deposed that he had made complete payment towards the discharge of his liability in cash but admittedly, he did not furnish any receipt for the cash payments C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.10/17 made by him or any other proof showing that the said liability stands discharged. It was therefore contended that the accused has been unable to rebut the presumption of liability. 14. The principal argument of the Ld. Counsel for accused was that the cheque in question was as per the case of the complainant itself, issued for the discharge of a time barred debt and as such it cannot be said to have been issued for discharge of a legally enforceable debt or other liability and therefore, offence u/s 138 NI Act is not made out. To substantiate this argument, the Ld. Counsel for accused referred to the testimony of the AR of the complainant/CW­1 in his affidavit Ex.CW1/A as well as during cross examination. The Ld. Counsel submitted that in Ex. CW1/A, the AR of the complainant has deposed as CW­1 that the last payment from the accused was received by the complainant in the month of April, 2014 and that the accused issued the cheque in question in the year 2019 which was dated 16.12.2019 upon the receipt of legal demand notice from the complainant. That the period of limitation for recovery of the amount has elapsed wayback in the year 2017 itself when counted even from the date of last default in April, 2014 onwards. On the other hand, the cheque in question was issued by the accused in 2019. As the alleged loan amount was recoverable uptill 2017, in 2019 it was clearly time barred debt, if not already paid by the accused as per the schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963 . A fortiori, if the complainant's case is accepted, the cheque in question was issued by the accused to discharge a time barred debt and time barred debt not being a legally enforceable liability, the dishonor of the cheque in question did not amount to offence C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.11/17 u/s 138 NI Act . 15. I find considerable force in the contention of the Ld. Counsel for the accused. As mentioned in paragraph 3, the explanation to section 138 NI Act provides that "for the purposes of section 138 , 'debt or other legal liability' means legally enforceable debt or other liability. It is a settled law that a time barred debt is not a legally recoverable debt within the meaning of section 138 NI Act and hence, in case of dishonour of a cheque issued against a time barred liability, the provisions of section 138 NI Act are not attracted. 16. During the cross examination as regards the period of limitation, CW­1 has denied the suggestion that no written communication took place between the complainant and accused from December 2014 till September 2019. However, he admitted that it is correct that no such alleged communication was placed on record by the complainant. Under such circumstances, the suggestion of Ld. Counsel for the accused, though denied by CW­1, that any such communication was not placed on record as there was no such communication by the complainant to the accused becomes relevant. CW­1 rather made another self­serving statement during his cross­examination that the complaianant did not took action against the accused from August 2014 till September 2019 as there were verbal communication between the complainant and accused. This version of CW­1 is not corroborated from any material on record. No such assertion has been made anywhere in the complaint or in the affidavit in evidence. He admitted that the cheque in question was handed C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.12/17 over by the accused to the complainant in the year 2019 itself and that it was signed in his presence by the accused. Therefore, it is manifest from the above circumstances that there is no written correspondence between the parties from the year 2014 till 2019 and that the complainant has presented for encashment the cheque in question which relates to the liability which was recoverable uptill the year 2017. It is not the case of the complainant that the accused had acknowledged his liability in writing towards the complainant in between this time period so as to start a fresh period of limitation against the accused. 17. Even otherwise in the present case, no document has come on record on behalf of the complainant to show that there was any acknowledgement of liability within the meaning of Section 18 of Limitation Act, 1963, on the part of the accused before the alleged amount became time barred in the year 2017. Even as per section 19 of Limitation Act, 1963, the limitation period for a debt is extended only if some payment is made towards the same before the limitation period ends. Again, in the present case, nothing has come on record to show that the accused had made any payment between 2014 and 2019. 18. It is pertinent to also mention that the proposition that dishonor of a cheque issued for discharge of a time barred debt or other liability does not tantamount to offence under section 138 of the NI Act is no longer res integra. In this regard, reliance is placed upon the judgment in the case titled Sasseriyil Joseph v. Devassia (order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court dated 10/01/2009) wherein, in a similar case, it has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that in view of the explanation to section 138 C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.13/17 of the NI Act , a cheque which has been issued by the accused for a debt which was barred by limitation, the penal provision under Section 138 of the NI Act is not attracted. 19. At this stage, it would be prudent to discuss the judgment M/s Jage Ram Karan Singh & Anr. Vs. State & Anr. (supra) relied upon by the Ld. Counsel of the accused which states that any cheque issued against a liability that was time barred as on date of issuance of cheque cannot said to have been issued in discharge of a legally enforceable debt or liability. The judgment at length discusses as to what would constitute of a "legally enforceable debt" and the importance of the Section 18 of Limitation Act, 1963 i.e. the fact of acknowledgement in writing for a time barred debt. The judgment goes on to state that mere issuance of cheque after prescribed period of limitation of the debt does not constitute a valid acknowledgement under Section 18 of Limitation Act and that it will not revive a time barred debt. Hence, the presumption contained in the Section 139 NI Act that the cheque has been issued for the discharge of a debt or liability stands rebutted in such cases. In the above case , Hon'ble Delhi High Court after quoting section 18 of Limitation Act, 1963 held that: 25. A bare perusal of the aforesaid provision clearly goes on to show that for analyzing the limitation of a liability beyond a period of three years, the acknowledgment, if any, must be there before the period of limitation is over, which is not the case in hand. 26. Further, it has been held time and again by the Apex Court as well as by the various High Courts that mere giving of a cheque, without anything more, will not revive a time­ barred debt, because cheque has to be given, as contemplated by the explanatory, in discharge of a legally C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.14/17 enforceable debt. In this regard, it may be relevant to take note of the order dated 10.9.2001 relied upon by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 titled Sasseriyil Joseph v. Devassia (supra) wherein, in a similar case, it has been held by the Supreme Court that, a cheque which has been issued by the accused for a due which was barred by limitation, the penal provision under Section 138 of the NI Act is not attracted. The relevant observations made in this regard in the aforesaid judgment are reproduced hereunder: ­ "We have heard learned counsel for the petitioner. We have perused the judgment of the High Court of Kerala in Criminal Appeal No. 161 of 1994 confirming the judgment/order of acquittal passed by the Addl. Sessions Judge, Thalassery in Criminal Appeal No. 212 of 1992 holding inter alia that the cheque in question having been issued by the accused for due which was barred by limitation the penal provision under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act is not attracted in the case. On the facts of the case as available on the records and the clear and unambiguous provision in the explanation to Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act the judgment of the lower appellate Court as confirmed by the High Court is unassailed. Therefore, the special leave petition is dismissed." 20. Reliance is also placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in M/s Vijay Polymers Pvt. Ltd. vs M/S Vinnay Aggarwal (Crl.M.C. 1682/2008 decided on 24/04/2009), wherein also it was held that, cheques issued for a time­barred debt would not fall within the definition of 'legally enforceable debt', which is the essential requirement for a complaint under Section 138 of the NI Act; the extended meaning of debt or liability has been explained in the Explanation to the Section which means a legally enforceable debt or liability. C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.15/17 21. Similarly, in Prajan Kumar Jain v. Ravi Malhotra , 2009 SCC Online Del 3368, it was held by Hon'ble Delhi High Court that, an acknowledgment to be encompassed within the ambit of Section 18 of the Limitation Act has to be an acknowledgment in writing as also within the prescribed period of limitation. These are the twin requirements which have to be fulfilled in order to be a valid acknowledgment under Section 18 of the Limitation Act. Relevant portion of the aforesaid judgment is reproduced hereunder: "10....This acknowledgment even as per the complaint was much after the statutory period of three years which is the prescribed period of limitation for the recovery of an outstanding amount. An acknowledgment to be encompassed within the ambit of Section 18 of the Limitation Act has to be an acknowledgment in writing as also within the prescribed period of limitation. These are the twin requirements which have to be fulfilled in order to be a valid acknowledgment under Section 18 of the Limitation Act which is admittedly not so in the instant case. In this case this acknowledgment to pay the balance amount was in terms of the settlement dated 26.1.2005 i.e. much after the statutory period of three years; it also does not speak of the acknowledgement being in writing. It was thus not a valid acknowledgment." 22. In light of the preceding discussion, it has to be held that the cheque in question was issued by the accused in the year 2019 on 16.12.2019 in connection with a debt/liability which has already become time barred in the year 2017. Hence the debt was not a legally recoverable debt in the year 2019 when the cheque in question was issued within the meaning of the term under section 138 NI Act. C.C. No. 1823/20 Raghav Aditya Chits Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Nazar Mohammad Page No.16/17 Therefore, offence u/s 138 NI Act is not proved against the accused. 23. Accordingly, the accused Nazar Mohammad is acquitted of the offence under section 138 of the N.I. Act. Bail bonds stands cancelled and surety, if any, stands discharged. File be consigned to record room after due compliance. Announced in the Open Court on 17th Day of March, 2023 (PANKAJ RAI) Metropolitan Magistrate­05, NI Act RAC/New Delhi/17.03.2023 C.C.
